subject: SLA carve-outs & maintenance window — proposed redlines and next steps
messages:
From: Danielle Ruiz <danielle.ruiz@stellarpay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@stellarpay.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: SLA carve-outs & maintenance window — initial ask

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the latency profile on Redwood. Our legal team reviewed the draft order form and raised two material items on the SLA appendix that we need clarified before we can proceed:

1) Maintenance window: The current draft allows for a 4-hour weekly maintenance window and a 6-hour emergency window. For our payments stack we need the agreed routine maintenance window reduced to a maximum of 2 hours per week and emergency maintenance limited to 3 hours unless we provide explicit approval.

2) Service credits cap: The redline caps service credits at 10% of monthly fees. Our procurement policy requires a hard cap of 5% and a mutual carve-out for scheduled maintenance that is notified 72 hours in advance.

Also, can we tighten P1 and P2 response SLA definitions — our ops team expects a P1 response within 1 hour and a P2 within 4 hours (not just acknowledgement).

I've attached the order form with inline comments (StellarPay_OrderForm_v3.docx) and a short note with our recommended SLA language. Happy to walk through this live — Alex and I are available Friday afternoon.

Thanks,
Danielle Ruiz
Head of IT Procurement, StellarPay

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ruiz <danielle.ruiz@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carve-outs & maintenance window — initial ask

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear note and the attachments.

We're aligned to move quickly. I looped in Kimberly (legal) and Aditya (product/ops) so we can evaluate the operational impact of the requested windows and caps. A few quick confirms from our side:
- We can prioritize a P1 operational response ladder that includes an initial substantive response within 1 hour; full mitigation timelines will depend on incident class.
- Maintenance windows are both an operational and contractual concern; Aditya will check whether routine tasks can be staged to keep routine maintenance <=2h in most regions.

Kimberly — can you review the proposed 5% cap + 72-hour scheduled maintenance carve-out and propose contract language we can share back to StellarPay? Aditya and I will validate the operational feasibility and propose fallback language if we need a little more breathing room (e.g., quarterly 4-hour blackout allowance with customer opt-in).

Danielle — would a short 30-minute call on Friday at 2:30pm PT work to align? If so, I can send a calendar invite and a one-page summary of proposed redline text before the call.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Danielle Ruiz <danielle.ruiz@stellarpay.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carve-outs & maintenance window — proposed legal language

Mina / team / Danielle — taking a pass at concrete contract text that maps to the asks. Inline below is the proposed replacement language for the SLA appendix. I'm sending this as a draft for discussion — product/ops notes welcome before we share as formal redline.

--- Proposed SLA appendix language (draft) ---
1) Maintenance windows: Redwood will provide no more than two (2) hours of scheduled maintenance per calendar week that may impact production availability in a given region. Emergency maintenance is limited to three (3) hours per event without Customer consent; Redwood will provide notice as soon as practicable and will obtain Customer approval for any extension. Scheduled maintenance will be communicated at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance.

2) Service credits: In the event Redwood fails to meet the Availability Target (as defined below), Customer may receive Service Credits up to a maximum of five percent (5%) of Fees for the applicable month in which the failure occurred. Service Credits shall not apply to downtime caused by: (a) Customer configured integrations or third-party services; (b) scheduled maintenance that was notified at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance; or (c) events of force majeure.

3) Response and resolution: Redwood will provide an initial substantive response to Severity 1 incidents within one (1) hour of Customer reporting. Severity 2 incidents will receive an initial substantive response within four (4) hours. Resolution time commitments will be qualified by incident complexity and Customer-provided diagnostics; Redwood will treat Severity 1 incidents as highest priority and will engage escalation engineers as required.

--- end draft ---

A few notes for operations: if we swallow the 2-hour weekly constraint without an opt-in carve for a quarterly upgrade, that will constrain some maintenance strategies (kernel/security patching, major model swaps). Aditya — do you want to propose a short fallback sentence (e.g., "quarterly non-overlapping maintenance up to 4 hours per quarter, subject to Customer opt-in")?

Danielle — if that language looks directionally correct we can produce a tracked-redline against your doc and route for signature. Happy to go on the Friday call to walk through.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
--Attachment: SLA_Appendix_diffs.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Danielle Ruiz <danielle.ruiz@stellarpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@stellarpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA carve-outs & maintenance window — proposed legal language

Kimberly / Mina,

Thanks — that draft is very helpful and aligns with our policies. A couple of tweak requests from StellarPay ops before we sign:

- Could you add an escalation ladder (names or roles acceptable) for Severity 1 incidents that describes a 1-hour touchpoint, 4-hour update cadence, and executive notification at 24 hours? We don't need individual names in the contract but a defined commitment helps with our internal post-incident reviews.
- For the service credits section, add wording that credits are the exclusive remedy for Availability failures (standard for us) and confirm credits will be applied to the next invoice.

We can discuss on the call — 2:30pm PT still works for Alex and me. Please send the invite.

Best,
Danielle
--Attachment: SP_Ops_ESC_Ladder.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Subject: Re: SLA carve-outs & maintenance window — action plan and artifacts

Thanks all — good call today. Summary and next steps:

1) Contract text: Kimberly will produce a tracked-change version of the Order Form and SLA appendix incorporating: (a) the 2-hour weekly scheduled maintenance limit + 72-hour notice; (b) 3-hour emergency maintenance limit; (c) 5% monthly service credit cap with carve-outs and "exclusive remedy" language; and (d) initial response SLAs + escalation ladder sketch. Expected delivery: Kimberly by EOD Tue 5/4.

2) Ops feasibility: Aditya confirmed routine model swaps and non-security patching can be staged to meet a 2-hour typical window; for major security updates we may request a customer opt-in for a quarterly 4-hour window. Aditya will include a short operational note that we will attach to the order form.

3) Signature flow: Mina will send a DocuSign envelope once legal and StellarPay agree to the redline. Anticipated DocuSign link provided here: https://docusign.com/DocuSign/Envelope12345

4) Artifacts: Attached are the two files we committed to circulate: the tracked redline (StellarPay_OrderForm_v3.docx with redlines) and the diff summary (SLA_Appendix_diffs.pdf). I've also uploaded our suggested escalation ladder to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSLA-redlines

If there are no further material changes after Kimberly's tracked redline, we will route for signatures on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
